records.title: Munda, Solomon Islands — ancestry and proposed selection

time.original: Research context: sampled individuals and genetic model ages have different temporal scopes.
time.method: Source-specific genomic analyses; no closed local occupation or language date inferred.
time.interpretation: Unplaced comparative evidence, not a Fiji highland settlement or dated language distribution.

claims.text: The study analyzed 21 Munda individuals from New Georgia in the western Solomon Islands; these are not Fiji-highland samples.
claims.explanation: Geographic scope matters before transferring population-specific results.

support.note: Geographic scope matters before transferring population-specific results.

claims.text: Munda HLA class II has elevated Papuan-related local ancestry; the authors favor selection but consider drift and recombination.
claims.explanation: Local-locus ancestry is not a whole-genome percentage or proof that a specified pathogen caused adaptation.

support.note: Local-locus ancestry is not a whole-genome percentage or proof that a specified pathogen caused adaptation.

review.summary: This comparative record keeps the studied population, ancestry model and interpretive limitations distinct from the Fiji-highland claims in the supplied synthesis.
review.limitations: Modern population study, not ancient Fiji DNA. Locus statistics are not resident population estimates, clinical predictions or universal adaptive history.
review.discussion: Ancestry estimates depend on reference populations, methods and sampling. Genetic affinity, language affiliation, archaeological culture and contemporary identity are distinct evidence types.
review.provenance: Independent review of five-page Lapita follow-up PDF and its 13 references. Working intake only; live v0.3.1 unchanged.

sourceRegister.title: How did Lapita-related admixture and later Austronesian gene flow shape Fiji Highlands?
sourceRegister.access: All five pages extracted with pypdf and read, including text, phase table, figure captions and 13-item bibliography. No copied figure image treated as new field data.
sourceRegister.note: The PDF identifies Consensus as its synthesis tool. Root archives the original file and complete extraction; this sidecar records reviewed facts only. No deployment authorized.

unresolved: No cited primary evidence reviewed here establishes a uniform 70–90% Papuan-related genome-wide ancestry proportion for Viti Levu highland groups. Obtain community-specific sampling, model definitions and tables before any such estimate.
Feldman (2026) full-text download failed. Its abstract supports distinct Fiji dispersals and a status/kinship association in one community, not a highland-wide lineage or climatic-isolation sequence.

The synopsis phase ranges 3000–2700, 2500–2000 and 2000–1200 BP are not accepted as synchronized Fiji highland occupation/genetic events. Model ages, sample dates and ceramic horizons need separate contextual chronologies.

AD 1300–1700 fortification and AD 1000–1800 Polynesian back-flow ranges need explicit local dates and archaeological/genomic evidence. Cochrane abstract alone does not supply them; Skoglund (2016) does not test AD 1300 climate-driven relocation.

The assertion that later Tongan voyagers strongly reshaped eastern Fiji while western highland clans remained isolated is not established by the accessed sources. No exact route, tribe boundary or ancestry gradient added.
Liu (2026) Palau dating depends on radiocarbon dietary/reservoir assumptions and model generation time. No fresh calibration performed and no detailed dated Palauan site distribution added.

Posth (2018) incremental process and Lipson (2018)/2020 demographic interpretations must remain separately attributed. Broad agreement on ancestry transformation does not settle its tempo or exact source-route history.

RIS semantic identity with existing Fiedel (2000) bibliography is confirmed; historical byte-for-byte identity cannot be established without the previous-upload checksum. Its 390 entries are references, not 390 reviewed studies.
corrections: The PDF question concerns Fiji highlands, but its cited populations span Vanuatu, Tonga, Palau, Micronesia and Munda. Findings cannot be transferred simply because all are Oceanian.

Early Vanuatu/Tonga individuals had little detectable Papuan-related ancestry. This does not demonstrate bypass of every Near Oceanian community or absence of early admixture throughout Remote Oceania; Palau differs.

Feldman (2026) later Polynesian-related gene flow around a millennium ago specifically concerns southern Vanuatu Outlier communities in the abstract; it does not independently date Fiji highland back-migration.
Isshiki (2020) sampled Munda, Solomon Islands. Elevated Papuan-related HLA local ancestry and proposed selection are not Fiji-highland genome-wide ancestry or direct proof of one endemic pathogen.
The reproduced Skoglund Extended Data Figure 3 shows Tongan admixture dates and Figure 4 models a 25% contribution to Tongans. New Guinean Highlander proxy is not a sample of Fiji highlanders.
Liu (2022) supports a Micronesian matrilocality interpretation. Matrilocal residence is not matrilineal descent or demonstrated uniform Pacific social organization.
Cochrane (2017) is a book chapter, now verified at Oxford, not an independently dated fortification survey. Burley (2013) is an argued polygenesis model; retain qualifications.
Lipson (2018) journal/preprint identifiers and Matisoo-Smith/Robins (2004) authorship corrected in the register. Rat mitochondrial genealogy is not human genomic admixture.
Fiedel (2000) RIS matches existing American-peopling bibliography context. It is unrelated to Fiji field evidence and is not the full Fiedel paper; no automatic new archaeological claim follows.
No resident counts, precisely bounded settlement/distribution dates, exact voyage paths, archaeological coordinates or language-divergence ages are inferred from these summaries.
